significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that epidemic TSFMs contain an internal signal coupled to sign(R_t−1) after curve momentum is held fixed, that this signal changes at the threshold near 1, and that manipulating it controls growth-versus-decline forecasts; the phrases "beyond what the recent curve shape/slope predicts" and "causally flips growth-vs-decline forecasts" make this a form-(iii) threshold/predictive coupling combined with a form-(ii) causal claim. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—opposite forecasts for matched-curve states—and a mechanism tying those forecasts to an R-threshold representation, thereby fixing expectations at ambiguous turning points rather than merely showing decodability; broad forecasters such as Chronos (Ansari et al., 2024) and TimesFM (Das et al., 2024) do not by their general forecasting objective guarantee this mechanistic coupling, while operational epidemiology work such as Cori et al. (2013) makes the threshold itself decision-relevant. A verified false primary claim would distinguish a momentum-based representation from a separable threshold mechanism and undermine mechanistic interpretations of these forecasts, although failure of steering alone would not rule out a distributed R_t representation, so the negative branch is informative but not uniquely explanatory. In the topic-substitution check, replacing the claim with the generic question of whether scientific mechanisms are represented would not earn this score; the exact R_t=1 transition under momentum matching is the claim-specific increment above the topic median.

reach.justification: The claim hands downstream users a "recovered 'R-threshold' direction" as an intervention and the design rule to "require explicit mechanistic (R_t-aware) validation before any TSFM is used for epidemic policy counterfactuals." This is ex ante rather than merely post hoc: it can audit or gate a forecasting model before its turning-point forecasts or policy counterfactuals are relied upon. Although the coordinates of the direction would require re-extraction per model, the substantive conclusion predicts that the internal and forecast transition will remain localized near R_t=1 after recalibration; the asserted scope covers epidemic TSFMs across general and epidemiology-aware model families, with uptake by developers, public-health model auditors, and policy-forecast users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic scientific-representation research supplies neither this pre-deployment gate nor the transferable threshold relation, so the reach comes from the claim rather than from the public-health topic itself.
